How to use this calculator

  1. Enter known measurement, measurement.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How circle is calculated

The circle relations are d=2r, circumference=2πr, and area=πr². If circumference or area is entered, radius is recovered before the other values are calculated. A circle with diameter 10 cm has circumference 10π ≈ 31.416 cm and area 25π ≈ 78.540 cm².

d=2r; circumference=2πr; area=πr².
A worked example

A circle with diameter 10 cm has circumference 10π ≈ 31.416 cm and area 25π ≈ 78.540 cm².

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

May a circumference or area be zero?

No; a zero-size circle has no positive radius.

Why is area in squared units while circumference is in ordinary units?

Area spans two dimensions; circumference measures a length around the boundary.
